title: Caring for Your Eyes
description: The final shards are near, but Umbra strikes at the one thing light needs — healthy eyes. Learn to protect the precious gift of sight.

content.value: Eyes are delicate and cannot be replaced like a torch bulb. A few simple habits keep them healthy for life. Professor Prism calls these 'the light-keeper's rules'.

✅ DO                          ❌ DON'T
Read in good light            Read in dim light or bright glare
Hold books ~25 cm away        Bring screens too close to eyes
Eat vitamin-A foods           Rub eyes with dirty hands
Wash eyes with clean water    Stare at the Sun or a laser
Get regular eye check-ups     Read in a moving vehicle

Sometimes the eye's lens does not focus light exactly on the retina. Someone with MYOPIA (short-sight) sees near objects clearly but distant ones are blurry. Someone with HYPERMETROPIA (long-sight) sees far objects clearly but nearby ones are blurry. Both are corrected with suitable spectacle lenses that help focus the light back onto the retina.

A diet lacking Vitamin A can cause night blindness — difficulty seeing in dim light. Foods like carrots, papaya, mango, spinach, milk and eggs are rich in Vitamin A and help keep the retina's rod cells healthy.
Never look directly at the Sun or point a laser at anyone's eyes — the intense light can permanently damage the retina, which cannot heal itself.
Key Takeaway: Protect your eyes with good light, safe distance, clean hands and Vitamin-A foods. Myopia and hypermetropia are focusing defects corrected with spectacle lenses.

quiz.question: A person with myopia (short-sight) has trouble seeing…
quiz.explain: In myopia, distant objects look blurry while near objects are clear. Spectacle lenses correct the focus.

quiz.question: Which habit is GOOD for your eyes?
options: Reading with the book about 25 cm away in good light
quiz.explain: Reading at a comfortable distance in good light reduces strain and keeps your eyes healthy.

quiz.question: A lack of which vitamin can cause night blindness?
quiz.explain: Vitamin A keeps the retina's rod cells healthy. Too little can cause night blindness. Carrots and spinach are rich in it.
